<section class="cb83 cb83v2 cb83credit cpad bgdarkslate" data-trackas="cb83" data-ocomid="cb83">
<div class="cb83w7 cwidth">
<div class="cb83w3">
<h1 class="herotitle txtwhite">Oracle Java SE Support Roadmap</h1>
<p class="cb83byline">(Updated September 15, 2026)</p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<!-- /CB83v2 -->
<!-- / _Raw-Text -->
<!-- _Raw-Text -->
<section class="cc01 cc01v0 cpad">
<div class="cc01w1 cwidth">
<p>Oracle provides this Oracle Java SE Support Roadmap, to help you understand maintenance and support options and related timelines. If you are looking for the latest free JDK release from Oracle, please see <a href="/java/technologies/downloads/" target="_blank">oracle.com/javadownload</a> or under an open source license, at <a href="http://jdk.java.net/" target="_blank">jdk.java.net</a>. Oracle also provides a separate support roadmap for features in the <a href="/java/technologies/jvp-support-roadmap.html" target="_blank">Oracle Java Verified Portfolio</a>, which is the collection of libraries, frameworks and tools that are fully supported for Oracle Customers.</p>
<p> In this roadmap:</p>
<p>
<strong>Oracle Customers</strong> are those Oracle customers with an active (1) <a href="/java/java-se-subscription/" target="_blank">Java SE Subscription product</a>, (2) support contract for Oracle Java SE Advanced, Oracle Java SE Advanced Desktop, Oracle Java SE Suite, and/or Java SE Support, (3) entitlement to Oracle Java as an Oracle Could Infrastructure customer, or (4) entitlement for use of Java SE solely with another Oracle product (Visit <a href="https://support.oracle.com/support/?kmContentId=1557737" target="_blank">[Java SE] Support Entitlement for Java SE When Used As Part of Another Oracle Product (KB827002)</a> – Requires Support Login).</p>
<p>
<strong>Personal, Development and other Users</strong> are those who use Java SE under one of the permitted uses at no cost under the <a href="/downloads/licenses/javase-license1.html" target="_blank">Oracle Technology Network License Agreement for Java SE</a>. This includes individuals who use Java SE for free on personal desktops or laptops, or those who use Java SE for development use. Please see the <a href="/java/technologies/javase/jdk-faqs.html" target="_blank">Oracle Java SE Licensing FAQ</a> for more information.</p>
<p>
<strong>All Users</strong> are those who use Java SE 21 and later at no cost under the terms of the <a href="/downloads/licenses/no-fee-license.html" target="_blank">Oracle No-Fee Terms and Conditions License</a>.</p>
<h4 id="jdkandopenjdk">Oracle JDK and OpenJDK builds from Oracle</h4>
<p>Since September 2017, Oracle provides Oracle OpenJDK releases under a free <a href="http://openjdk.java.net/legal/gplv2+ce.html" target="_blank">open source license</a> (similar to that of Linux). Availability and community support of OpenJDK releases provided by Oracle is listed separately on <a href="http://jdk.java.net/" target="_blank">jdk.java.net</a>. </p>
<p>Oracle JDK 21 is approaching the end of permissive licensing.  Update releases of Oracle JDK 21 released beginning with the October 2026 Critical Patch Update (CPU) are planned to be offered under the Java SE OTN license, the same license under which we currently offer updates to Java 8, 11, and 17.</p>
<p>Since September 2025, Oracle provides the Oracle JDK 25 under a <a href="/downloads/licenses/no-fee-license.html" target="_blank">free use license</a> for All Users. Update releases of Oracle JDK 25 released after September of 2028 are planned to be offered under the Java SE OTN license, the same license under which we currently offer updates to Java 8, 11, and 17.</p>
<p>Oracle JDK releases for Java 8, 11, and 17 are available under the <a href="/downloads/licenses/javase-license1.html" target="_blank">Oracle Technology Network License Agreement for Java SE</a>, which is free for Personal, Development and other Users only.</p>
<p>For more information on Oracle Java licensing, please see the <a href="/java/technologies/javase/jdk-faqs.html" target="_blank">Oracle Java SE Licensing FAQ</a>.</p>
<p>Dates listed below apply only to the commercially supported Oracle JDK releases available to Oracle Customers.</p>
<h4 id="javase">Oracle Java SE Product Releases</h4>
<p>Oracle provides Customers with Oracle Premier Support on Oracle Java SE products as described in the <a href="/support/lifetime-support/" target="_blank">Oracle Lifetime Support Policy</a>. For product releases after Java SE 8, Oracle will provide Long-Term-Support (LTS) on specific releases. Java SE 8, 11, 17, 21, and 25 are LTS releases. Oracle intends to make future LTS releases every two years meaning the next planned LTS release is Java 29 in September 2027. For the purposes of Oracle Premier Support, non-LTS releases are considered a cumulative set of implementation enhancements of the most recent LTS release. Once a new feature release is made available, any previous non-LTS release will be considered superseded. For example, Java SE 9 was a non-LTS release and immediately superseded by Java SE 10 (also non-LTS), Java SE 10 in turn was immediately superseded by Java SE 11. Java SE 11 however is an LTS release, and therefore Oracle Customers will receive Oracle Premier Support and periodic update releases, even after Java SE 12 was released.</p>
<p> Examples of some key product dates for Oracle Java SE product offerings include:</p>

<h4 id="eopu8">End of Permissive Licensing of Java SE 8</h4>
<p>Java SE 8 has gone through the <a href="https://blogs.oracle.com/java/end-of-public-updates-is-a-process-not-an-event" target="_blank">End of Permissive Licensing process</a> for legacy releases in April, 2019. Oracle will continue to provide free public updates and auto updates of Java SE 8 indefinitely for Personal, Development and other Users via <a href="https://www.java.com/en/download/" target="_blank">java.com</a>. Oracle intends to provide at least 18 months notice on this page and other communication channels if an end of availability date is set. Developers can find <a href="/java/technologies/downloads/" target="_blank">Oracle Java SE updates, including Oracle Java SE 8, 11, 17, 21, and current releases, on OTN</a>. As of the April 16, 2019 <a href="/security-alerts/" target="_blank">quarterly critical patch update</a>, Oracle Customers should access updates to Java SE 8 for commercial use from Oracle through My Oracle Support and via auto update where applicable (Visit <a href="https://support.oracle.com/support/?kmContentId=11123885" target="_blank">Supported Java SE Downloads on MOS (KA961)</a> – Requires Support Login).</p>
<p>Oracle does not plan to migrate desktops from Java SE 8 to later versions via the auto update feature. This includes the Java Plugin and Java Web Start. Instead of relying on a browser-accessible system JRE, we encourage application developers to <a href="https://blogs.oracle.com/java/the-future-of-javafx-and-other-java-client-roadmap-updates" target="_blank">use the packaging options introduced since Java SE 9</a> to repackage and deliver their Java applications as stand-alone applications that include their own custom runtimes.</p>
<h4 id="eopl17">End of Permissive Licensing of Java SE 17</h4>
<p>Java SE 17 was released in September of 2021 and public updates through September of 2024 were under a <a href="/downloads/licenses/no-fee-license.html" target="_blank">permissive license</a>. Further update releases of Oracle JDK 17, released as of October 15, 2024 are available under the <a href="https://www.java.com/otnlicense" target="_blank">Java SE OTN license</a>, the same license under which we currently offer updates to Java 8 and 11. Users wanting to continue with permissively licensed versions of Java should move to Oracle JDK 25 or later.</p>
<h4 id="eopl21">End of Permissive Licensing of Java SE 21 (Sept 2026) approaching</h4>
<p>The release of JDK 25 LTS in September of 2025 started the one-year overlap period for users relying on JDK 21 LTS under a <a href="/downloads/licenses/no-fee-license.html" target="_blank">permissive license</a> to update to JDK 25. Updates of JDK 21 released beginning with the October 2026 Critical Patch Update (CPU), are planned to be offered under the <a href="https://www.java.com/otnlicense" target="_blank">Java SE OTN license</a>.</p>
<p>Users wanting to continue with permissively licensed versions of Java after October of 2026 should upgrade to Oracle JDK 25 or later.</p>
<h4 id="webandjavafx">Web Deployment Technology</h4>
<p>The Web Deployment Technology bundled with the Oracle JRE, consisting of the Java Plugin and Java Web Start has a shorter support lifecycle: only five years of Premier Support. The deployment stack was marked as deprecated and flagged for removal in Java SE 9 and Java SE 10. Oracle Java SE 11 and later versions do not include the Deployment Stack. Java SE 8 will be the sunset release for the Deployment Stack Oracle extended support of Java Web Start on Java SE 8 until the end of Java SE 8 Extended Support. The Java Plugin (Java Applets) remains updated in Java 8, but may be removed at any time in a future release.  Oracle Customers can find more information at <a href="https://support.oracle.com/support/?kmContentId=2511148" target="_blank">Java SE 8 End of Java Plugin Support (PNEWS2519)</a> (requires login).</p>
<p>Java SE 8 is the recommended and only supported version of the deployment stack. The Java deployment technology will not be supported beyond Java SE 8. See the <a href="/support/lifetime-support/" target="_blank">Oracle Lifetime Support Policy</a> for details.</p>
<h4 id="EndGraal">End of support for GraalVM in Java SE Products</h4>
<p>GraalVM for JDK 24 was the final version of GraalVM licensed and supported as part of Oracle Java SE Products. Any entitled customers seeking patches or updates to previously released GraalVM versions should download them through <a href="https://support.oracle.com/" target="_blank">My Oracle Support (MOS)</a>. More information is available on <a href="https://blogs.oracle.com/java/post/detaching-graalvm-from-the-java-ecosystem-train" target="_blank">this blog</a>. Customers seeking additional information or assistance should contact <a href="https://support.oracle.com/" target="_blank">My Oracle Support (MOS)</a>.</p>
<h4 id="jipher">Jipher</h4>
<p>Jipher is now supported as part of the Java Verified Portfolio. Future Jipher roadmap information will be part of the Oracle Java Verified Portfolio roadmap.</p>
<br/>
<p> * Oracle Java SE product dates are provided as <strong>examples</strong> to illustrate the support policies. Customers should refer to the <a href="/support/lifetime-support/" target="_blank">Oracle Lifetime Support Policy</a> for the most up-to-date information. Timelines may differ for Oracle Products with a Java SE dependency (<a href="https://support.oracle.com/support/?kmContentId=1557737" target="_blank">[Java SE] Support Entitlement for Java SE When Used As Part of Another Oracle Product (KB827002)</a> – Requires Support Login).</p>
<p> ** These support timelines apply to Java client and server deployments of Java with the exception of Web Deployment Technology and JavaFX. For more information on those features, see below.</p>

The Extended Support uplift fee will be waived for the period March 2022 – December 2030 for Java SE 8. During this period, you will receive Extended Support as described in the Oracle Technical Support Level sections of the Technical Support Policies.</p>

Temurin™ Support

Support

  • Overview

Community Support

We are prepared to stand behind our release quality binaries, so each build that is identified as a release receives support via the Adoptium® community. Our support means that you can raise an issue to describe a bug you have found in the build, and we will work with you and the appropriate development team to resolve it. Any fixes we identify will be delivered as part of the next Adoptium release.

As a community of open source developers, our commitment is to triage any issues raised and champion them in the appropriate source code project. Of course, if the problem arises from the way we build and test the code we can fix that directly. For dedicated support with service level agreements, you should contact commercial companies offering support on Temurin binaries. Read Java Is Still Free (3.0.0) for some background information about Java support options.

Commercial Support

We understand that some users prefer commercial, paid-for support of Eclipse Temurin. Eclipse does not provide such services but please see our Commercial Support page where a list of companies offering contracted support is maintained.

Release Roadmap

The frequency of Temurin releases is guided by the schedule of our dependencies.

OpenJDK provide a new feature release every six months, and a maintenance/security update based upon each active release every three months. The release dates for those from the OpenJDK project are typically the third Tuesday of January, April, July and October. We will follow this schedule for publishing binary releases from Adoptium to ensure you get the latest, most secure builds.

In addition, every two years since 2021 one feature release will be designated as a Long Term Supported (LTS) release. We will support LTS releases for at least four years. This assurance will allow you to stay on a well-defined code stream, and give you time to migrate to the next, new, stable, LTS release when it becomes available.

When OpenJDK chooses to produce a CSPU release in order to address security issues, Adoptium will also produce a release. These will typically take place on the third Tuesday of a month that does not already contain a release. Expected CSPUs are listed [here](https://ops.java/releases/), where the version strings have four numbers each (e.g. 25.0.5.1) instead of three.

Based upon this roadmap, here is the timetable showing the current release dates of the various OpenJDK releases used to build Eclipse Temurin. Note that the dates below are from the upstream OpenJDK project page and should not be considered the date which the Adoptium project will have binaries available - there will be a short delay relative to these dates while we complete our extensive build and test cycles which can take up to three weeks. We always prioritise the most popular platforms which will typically appear within a few days of these dates.
